pairs.subject: prompt-assembly
pairs.evidence: src/lib/scoring/prompt.ts:91 The scoring rubric in model.ts is rendered by one pure assembler with a byte-stable SYSTEM prefix, and its version is folded into the cache key, but the standing text opens on an expertise and competence claim ('an expert assessor', 'rigorous', 'don't be shy'), which is the priming task-envelope says to replace.

techniques.evidence: src/lib/scoring/prompt.ts:91 The prompt opens with an expertise and competence claim. The rest of the line (never invent facts, JSON only) is a real constraint and the TASK block gives a done shape, but the competence priming is the pattern the technique says to remove.

src/lib/scoring/prompt.ts:458 Role, then rubric, then task contract, composed once as the stable SYSTEM. Per-repo data goes only in the user message. Callers (bedrock.ts, claude-cli.ts) pass typed LlmScoreInput, never prompt text.

src/lib/scoring/prompt.ts:546 One cut, between the byte-identical system prefix and the per-repo user message. Volatile blocks (decisions, craft ladder) are deliberately kept out of SYSTEM so they don't break the cache.

src/lib/maturity/model.ts:342 The rubric and prompt version is folded into the scan cache key (cache.ts makeCacheKey). model.test.ts pins a hash of the SYSTEM prompt, so a prompt change that skips the bump fails the test.

src/lib/scoring/prompt.ts:116 The file window has a per-file cap, a whole-window cap and a reserved workflow quota. Omitted files are named to the model (WINDOW COVERAGE) and truncation leaves a marker. The caps are counted in characters, not derived tokens.
src/lib/scoring/prompt.ts:525 Absent values render a declared default. Repo-authored spans are neutralized and the bulk sits inside the UNTRUSTED fence.
src/lib/scoring/prompt.ts:103 The product's own level and dimension terms are rendered from the model.ts authority into the standing prefix.
src/lib/scoring/prompt.ts:428 The scorer has no tools. The claim-facet output contract is rendered from the claims.ts table rather than hand-written.
src/lib/scoring/prompt.ts:516 The per-commit prefix is a shared constant imported from its consumer, the claims verifier, so the consumer can be named.
src/lib/scoring/prompt.ts:524 Assembly reads no clock. The only date is the repo's push time, passed in as data.
src/lib/scoring/prompt.ts:464 Single-shot system plus user call with no transcript and no tools, so the compaction, continuation and elision techniques do not apply.

src/lib/scoring/prompt.ts:464 No tool loop or history to elide; the model can't refetch anyway. The earlier stale verdict counted character-slicing against this, but the window now names omitted files to the model.

pairs.subject: prompt-assembly
pairs.evidence: src/lib/org/followups.ts:689 buildAgentBrief takes the finished string from buildFixPrompt and appends the org standard and working perimeter after it, so policy-class layers trail the per-call task outside any single assembler's ordering or budget, the post-return append the golden path says the door must seal against.

techniques.evidence: src/lib/org/followups.ts:688 Appends onto an already-assembled prompt string. The standard and perimeter (standing, policy-like) land after the volatile item list instead of leading it.

src/lib/org/followups.ts:273 The lane's capability and gate-surface rules are hand-written prose that copies the regexes in lane-gate-diff.ts. The comments record three measured drifts and no test ties the two together.

src/lib/org/followups.ts:638 Titles, rationale and explore questions are prior model output, so untrusted, but they are interpolated raw. Only failure output goes through neutralize, though the scoring prompt neutralizes the same craft titles for this exact threat. Absent perimeter values do get declared defaults.
src/lib/org/followups.ts:595 No expertise claim. Locate (read the repo's guidance) and Done (RESOLVED/SKIPPED lines) are present, but no explicit read-the-artifact check before reporting.
src/lib/org/followups.ts:541 Defines the house terms gap and rung and marks each item with one.
src/lib/org/followups.ts:652 The builder reads no clock; the date is a declared ctx input and goes in the tail.
src/lib/org/followups.ts:457 Produces one standalone brief and holds no transcript.
